institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important to me that the city was one I wanted to experience. That I had a sense of security, that there was a good study environment, and that I could get an Erasmus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the university I was going to attend gave good information. However, I think many things were unclear about mobility-online, OLA, etc. Difficult systems, and sometimes not so good instructions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was no direct assistance, but there was an introductory week for exchange students, where you had the opportunity to meet others and also received a lot of information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. I found it via a rental website, where there were several options. The university I studied at couldn't offer student housing for students from the Nordic countries, which was a bit of a shame, and they generally couldn't help us find a place to live - luckily I found something quickly.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you can, I would recommend living on campus, but if you can't, be out well in advance and research the area well if you have more alternatives.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a long and somewhat troublesome process. Fortunately, you can get help with registration, but I would definitely recommend that you sit down well in advance and look into it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to them. It could take days for them to respond, which could be frustrating, so again, be out there well in advance and maybe ask someone who has been there before or is going there.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went well. I got all the subjects I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be out in good time, familiarize yourself with things.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Since I'm on my bachelor's, I was only allowed to take equivalent courses for my bachelor's. I took four different subjects and although they were all the same level, they varied a lot in difficulty, etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Several of the subjects were very different, but it also depends on what degree you are taking. I am used to "classroom teaching", where you are expected to participate, do group work, etc. - there was really none of that here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Childhood studies, Introduction to Norwegian history, personality psychology and social psychology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all. But the psychology courses was difficult and challenging - but interesting!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You must be prepared for the fact that there will be a lot of expenses in the beginning, especially associations, memberships, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Many people think Norway is expensive, but it's actually not that expensive - very similar to Denmark. Transportation is much cheaper, shopping, fitness. On the other hand, food is a bit more expensive and restaurants are a bit more expensive - but not much more expensive than Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had a lot of different associations. There is something for everyone. In general, the city is known for being a student city and there is a hugely good student life with lots of opportunities for different activities for students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Erasmus Student Network has a lot of cool trips. Their associations also have a lot of different things. They had some cool fitness centers with a lot of different fun teams, and then they have the Student Society, where everything happens (everything from concerts, music quizzes, lectures, etc.)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips outside the city. There is a lot of beautiful nature to experience. Stay in a cabin, hike, ski, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since Norway and Denmark are very similar to each other, it was very easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Associations through NTNUI and "Studentersamfundet"

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anyone at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found the Norwegians very welcoming, smiling and helpful. They are very active and "healthy", which I also found inspiring.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Spend your free time in the nature around you, spend a lot of time at the "Studentersamfundet", take advantage of the fact that it is a city with a lot of students - feel the student life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not immediately, no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Not immediately, no.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found the exam period tough. I'm not used to having four different exams, so it was challenging. I quickly got along with other students from my "home university", so I didn't find socializing, which can normally be difficult, so challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
